page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
2 1938
"Found Slain
Margaret Veksler
Inquest Over
Slain Girl's
Body Is Held
Hearing Conducted In
Camera; Funeral
Services Today
The preliminary inquest over the body of Margaret Veksler, 21-year-old Russian emigre of the Jewish faith, whose dead body was discovered last Friday evening in the apartment of Captain H. M. Smyth, O.B.E., Assistant Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, was opened in the Kiaochow Road public mortuary yesterday morning.
The hearing, which lasted throughout the morning, was conducted strictly in camera, and was confined largely to the evidence given by Captain Smyth and a hotel boy of the Broadway Mansions.
The deceased is survived by a mother and a young child, both in Harbin. It is reported that Captain Smyth has already sent a cable to Harbin informing the mother of the tragedy.
Yesterday's inquest was attended by representatives of the Shanghai Municipal Police, including one of the Assistant Commissioners. However, a Miss Polly Bochman, the only person close to the deceased residing in Shanghai, was not permitted to attend the inquest, and the reason for this could not be ascertained.
Funeral Services Today
Due to the religious belief of the deceased, her funeral services will be held today at the Balkal Road Jewish Cemetery. It is the Jewish custom for burials to take place by sundown, not more than one day after death. It is understood that arrangements have been made for the services to be held this afternoon, when a Rabbi from the Jewish Synagogue will officiate.
According to the only available police information last night, detectives are working on the theory that Miss Veksler was murdered by Captain Smyth's houseboy. It was revealed that there was some evidence to show that the assailant had struggled violently with the deceased.
Came Here Five Years Ago
Miss Veksler, it was learnt yesterday, arrived in Shanghai about five years ago when she studied for about a year in the Public School for Girls.
Not long afterwards she married Alfred Haimovitch and they were subsequently understood to have separated. For a time she was employed in a cafeteria establishment known as "Kleinermann's" on Avenue Joffre. It was stated that she first knew Captain Smyth about two years ago.
The murder was committed between 4.30 and 5.30 o'clock Friday afternoon, her body being discovered with wounds in the head lying on the floor by Captain Smyth when he returned from police headquarters. The two had arranged to meet at the flat to discuss a trip which Miss Veksler was expected to take to England, to meet Captain Smyth's family.
When Captain Smyth arrived at the apartment he found it locked and consequently called the floor boy of the hotel for a key. The boy opened the door, and it was then that the gruesome discovery was made.
It is understood that the remains of Miss Veksler will be interred in a special section of the Jewish cemetery reserved for those who have met their death by violence.

《字林西报》。
1938年2月
“发现被杀
玛格丽特·韦克斯勒
对被杀少女尸体的死因研讯已举行
听证秘密进行；今日举行葬礼
昨日上午，在胶州路公共殓房，就21岁的犹太裔俄国移民玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Veksler）的尸体开启了初步死因研讯。她的尸体于上周五晚在上海公共租界工部局警务处助理总监、大英帝国勋章获得者H. M. 史密斯（H. M. Smyth）上尉的公寓内被发现。
整个上午进行的听证会严格秘密进行，主要局限于史密斯上尉和百老汇大厦一名侍役所提供的证词。
死者留有一位母亲和一个年幼的孩子，均在哈尔滨。据悉，史密斯上尉已致电哈尔滨，将这一悲剧告知其母。
昨日的死因研讯有上海公共租界工部局警务处的代表出席，其中包括一位助理总监。然而，波莉·博赫曼（Polly Bochman）小姐——死者在上海唯一的亲近之人——未被允许出席死因研讯，其原因无法查明。
今日举行葬礼
鉴于死者的宗教信仰，其葬礼将于今日在倍开尔路（Balkal Road）犹太公墓举行。根据犹太习俗，埋葬须在死后不超过一天、日落之前进行。据了解，仪式安排在今日下午举行，届时将由犹太会堂的一位拉比主持。
根据警方昨晚掌握的仅有信息，侦探们正依据以下推论开展工作：韦克斯勒小姐系被史密斯上尉的家仆谋杀。据透露，有一些证据表明，袭击者曾与死者发生过剧烈搏斗。
五年前来沪
据悉，韦克斯勒小姐约于五年前抵达上海，曾在公立女子学校（Public School for Girls）就读约一年。
不久后，她嫁给了阿尔弗雷德·海莫维奇（Alfred Haimovitch），随后据信两人分居。她一度受雇于霞飞路上一家名为“克莱纳曼”（Kleinermann's）的茶室。据说，她大约在两年前初次结识史密斯上尉。
谋杀案发生在周五下午4时30分至5时30分之间，史密斯上尉从警察总局返回时，发现韦克斯勒小姐头部受伤，躺在地板上。两人原约定在公寓见面，商讨韦克斯勒小姐预期前往英国拜访史密斯上尉家人的行程。
当史密斯上尉到达公寓时，发现房门紧锁，遂叫来酒店楼层侍役取钥匙。侍役打开门后，这才发现了这一可怕的景象。
据悉，韦克斯勒小姐的遗体将安葬在犹太公墓中专为死于暴力者保留的特殊区域。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
OCT 24 1931
Inquest Held
In Murder Of
Young Lady
Police Still Trying To
Locate Roomboy Who
Is Implicated
SERVICES TO BE HELD
HERE THIS MORNING

The inquest into the death of
Margaret Veksler, 21-year-old
Russian Jewess, who was found
murdered on Friday evening in
the Broadway Mansions flat of
Captain H. M. Smyth, O.B.E.,
Assistant Commissioner of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, was
held at the public mortuary
in Kiaochow Road yesterday
morning.
It is understood that evidence was
given by Captain Smyth himself
and by one of the roomboys em-
ployed at the Broadway Mansions.
The inquest was attended by re-
presentatives of the Shanghai
Municipal Police including one of
the Assistant Commissioners. The
hearing was opened at 10.15 o'clock
and lasted for several hours.

Police Theory

The police stated yesterday that
they were working on the theory
that Miss Veksler had been mur-
dered by Captain Smyth's houseboy.
There was evidence to show that a
struggle of a violent nature had
occurred between Miss Veksler and
her assailant, it was stated.
In the meantime efforts are being
made to locate the roomboy who is
said to have absconded, but it is
hoped that this task will be facil-
itated in view of the rigid control
being maintained in Hongkew. It
is necessary for all Chinese in that
area to carry passes bearing a com-
plete identification.
Additional information regarding
Miss Veksler was made available
here yesterday when it was stated
that she had been a resident of
Shanghai for about five years and
is survived by her mother now liv-
ing in Harbin. Miss Veksler stud-
ied at the Public School for Girls
here for two years but had few
close friends in Shanghai.

Jewish Custom Respected

It is understood that the mother
has been notified and that funeral
services will be held at 10.30 o'clock
this morning at the Jewish Ceme-
tery in Baikal Road. In order that
the Jewish custom which stipulates
that burial must take place without
delay might be complied with,
efforts were made to complete the
inquest yesterday. It is understood
that the remains will be interred
in a special section of the Jewish
cemetery reserved for those who
have met their death by violence.
Miss Veksler was murdered be-
tween 4.30 and 5.30 o'clock on Fri-
day afternoon, her body having
been discovered by Captain Smyth
when he returned home from police
headquarters. Captain Smyth, it is
stated, had planned to discuss with
her a trip which she was taking to
England, during the course of
which she planned to visit his
family.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1931年10月24日
举行年轻女士
谋杀案死因研讯
警方仍在试图 locating
涉案房间侍役
今晨在此举行葬礼

关于21岁的俄国犹太女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒的死因研讯已于昨日上午在胶州路公共殓房举行。她于周五晚在上海公共租界工部局警务处助理总监、大英帝国勋章获得者H. M. 史密斯（H. M. Smyth）上尉位于百老汇大厦的公寓内被发现遭谋杀。
据悉，史密斯上尉本人及百老汇大厦雇用的一名房间侍役提供了证词。上海公共租界工部局警务处的代表出席了死因研讯，其中包括一位助理总监。听证会于10时15分开始，持续了数小时。

警方推论

警方昨日表示，他们正依据以下推论开展工作：韦克斯勒小姐系被史密斯上尉的家仆谋杀。据称，有证据表明，韦克斯勒小姐与袭击者之间曾发生性质剧烈的搏斗。
与此同时，警方正努力寻找据称已潜逃的房间侍役，但鉴于虹口地区维持着严格的管制，希望此项工作能得以便利。该地区的所有中国居民必须携带载有完整身份信息的通行证。
昨日此处公布了关于韦克斯勒小姐的更多资料，称她在上海居住约五年，留有一位现居哈尔滨的母亲。韦克斯勒小姐曾在此地的公立女子学校就读两年，但在上海几乎没有亲密朋友。

尊重犹太习俗

据悉，其母已获通知，葬礼将于今晨10时30分在倍开尔路（Baikal Road）犹太公墓举行。为了遵守犹太习俗中关于必须立即下葬的规定，警方努力于昨日完成死因研讯。据悉，遗体将安葬在犹太公墓中专为死于暴力者保留的特殊区域。
韦克斯勒小姐于周五下午4时30分至5时30分之间被谋杀，史密斯上尉从警察总局回家时发现了她的尸体。据称，史密斯上尉原计划与她商讨她前往英国的行程，期间她计划拜访他的家人。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

OCT 19 1938

VERDICT ON VEKSLER
KILLER TO-DAY

Heavy Penalty For Cook
Expected; Reburial Of
Girl Not Definite

The fate of Yu Yen-yuen, 20-
year-old cook-boy, who confessed
to having murdered Miss Margaret
Veksler, 22-year-old Russian, in
the apartment of Captain E. M.
Smyth, O.B.E., Deputy Commis-
sioner of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, at Broadway Mansions on
September 30, this year, will be
made known this morning when
Judge Wong will deliver his ver-
dict at the First Special District
Court.

There have been two hearings of
the trial since it was opened about
two weeks ago, following the
arrest of the accused, who, at both
sessions, confessed his guilt to the
crime and related what had hap-
pened.

The accused told the Court that
he had been scolded by the deceas-
ed, after which he struck her
on the nose with a long knife. He
denied, however, that he had taken
a bottle of beer out of the refri-
gerator. He stated that Miss Veks-
ler had taken it out, but admitted
that he had struck her on the head
with it.

In his final summing-up, the
prosecutor, Assistant Municipal
Advocate T. Y. Chang, contended
that the murder had been pre-
meditated and that there was no
question of self-defence. He asked
that severe punishment be meted
out to the accused. Mr. Pao
Ching, attorney for the defence,
pleaded for leniency, stating that
the accused had no previous con-
victions and that the crime was
committed in a fit of rage.

Meanwhile, earlier statements
that the deceased, Margaret Veks-
ler, would be reburied in the
Baikal Road Jewish Cemetery fol-
lowing the present Jewish festivals,
could not be confirmed yesterday,
although it is understood that the
girl's mother, Mrs. Mordohovich,
has declared to Jewish officials here
that her daughter was of the Jew-
ish faith and requested, therefore,
that her reburial be held at the
Baikal Road Cemetery.

《上海泰晤士报》。

1938年10月19日

今日将对韦克斯勒
案凶手作出判决

预计厨师将面临重罚；
少女改葬事宜尚未确定

今年9月30日，20岁的厨役余仁元（Yu Yen-yuen，音译）承认在上海公共租界工部局警务处副总监、大英帝国勋章获得者E. M. 史密斯（E. M. Smyth）上尉位于百老汇大厦的公寓内谋杀了22岁的俄国女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Veksler）。今晨，黄法官将在第一特区地方法院宣判，届时余仁元的命运将揭晓。

自约两周前被告被捕并开庭以来，庭审已进行了两次。在这两次庭审中，被告均承认罪行并陈述了事发经过。

被告告诉法庭，他遭到死者斥责，随后用一把长刀刺击其鼻子。然而，他否认从冰箱中取出一瓶啤酒。他声称是韦克斯勒小姐自己取出的，但他承认曾用该酒瓶击打其头部。

在最后总结陈词中，公诉人、市公署助理律师张T. Y.（T. Y. Chang，音译）主张，该谋杀系预谋所致，不存在自卫情节。他要求对被告处以严厉惩罚。辩护律师鲍静（Pao Ching，音译）请求从轻发落，称被告无前科，且犯罪是在盛怒之下所为。

与此同时，此前有关死者玛格丽特·韦克斯勒将在当前犹太节日过后改葬于倍开尔路（Baikal Road）犹太公墓的说法，昨日未能得到证实。尽管据悉，女孩的母亲莫尔多霍维奇夫人（Mrs. Mordohovich，音译）已向此间的犹太官员声明，其女信奉犹太教，因此请求将其改葬于倍开尔路公墓。

Wexler Killer
Jailed For Life
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY, OCT 19 1938
Chinese Cook Receives
Sentence; Prisoner
Remains Calm

Yu Yih-yuen, 21-year-old cook-boy, was sentenced to life imprisonment by Judge Wong in the First Special District Court this morning, for the murder of Miss Margaret Wexler, 22, Russian, at Broadway Mansions on September 30. He was also deprived of his civil rights for life. He will serve the sentence in Ward Road Jail.

The effeminate cookboy took the decision calmly. He did not file notice of appeal today, but is expected that he will appeal against the decision in the high Chinese court.

In Police Quarter
The youthful boy, who is a native of Tinghai in Chekiang, murdered Miss Wexler in the living quarters of Captain H. M. Smyth, deputy commissioner of the S.M.P., on the afternoon of September 30, after a quarrel over bad eggs.

The cookboy made a full confession upon his arrest six days after the murder, both at the police station and in open court. It required only two court sessions to conclude the case.

Details Given
Detailed particulars concerning the crime were given at the court both by the convicted cookboy and by Mr. T. Y. Chang, municipal advocate, who brought a charge of premeditated murder against him during the first hearing. It was brought out during the trial that Yu had been in the employ of Captain Smyth since July last year.

Motive Said Revenge
The actual murder was prompted by revenge, it was stated. Frequently scolded by Miss Wexler for his alleged slack habits, the cookboy was not on friendly terms with the victim, he said. On the day of murder, he was scolded several times for having purchased bad eggs, resulting in a quarrel during which both resorted to rough-house tactics. He stated that he killed her because he was afraid that she might tell Captain Smyth about the fighting in the apartment.

An altercation between the boy and Miss Wexler took place at about 8 o'clock on the morning of September 30. While serving both Captain Smyth and Miss Wexler at breakfast, he was reprimanded by the latter for bringing in bad eggs. He offered no argument, he stated.

Bought Eggs
Captain Smyth left for his office after breakfast and Yu was told to buy eggs at the market by Miss Wexler. About 10 o'clock, one Mrs. Jay Dukoff paid a call on Miss Wexler. They went out together to buy a box of chocolates and Miss Wexler returned within an hour alone.

While Yu was cleaning up the bedroom, Miss Wexler is alleged to have scolded him again for not having picked up soiled silk panties from under the bed. At about this time, a telephone call came from one of the cook's relatives. Again Miss Wexler was said to have been angry for his use of the telephone.

Had Fight
Miss Wexler followed the boy to the kitchen where she picked up a damaged egg from the window sill and allegedly accused the boy of having bought bad eggs. The latter retorted and snatched the egg away from Miss Wexler. Angered by this she allegedly struck the boy, who fought back by hitting her with the handle of a meat knife.

Threatening to tell Captain Smyth about the incident, Miss Wexler is alleged to have telephoned to a friend in Russian. It was later ascertained that Miss Wexler had telephoned Mrs. Dukoff.

She then returned to the living room and read a magazine. It was about 12.30 o'clock. The cook was again called in and this time he was allegedly scolded for not having dusted a table properly. At this time blood was trickling from her nose.

Struggle On Floor
She suddenly noticed the blood and allegedly again attacked the boy. Both struggled on the floor for some time during which Miss Wexler bit the boy's finger and scratched his face and in turn had her hand bitten. The weaker of the two, Miss Wexler ceased to struggle.

The boy returned to the kitchen and took out a full pint bottle of beer from the refrigerator and went into the living room again. He hit her five or six times on the head with it. He crossed the room and pulled down the blind. Then he took out a big piece of blotting paper and wrote eight Chinese characters, meaning: "If you do not succeed in injuring others, you will injure yourself."

Took Money, Watch
At this juncture he heard the woman gasp. Alarmed, he found a piece of canvas string and tied it around her neck. Then he covered the body with a towel and a blanket. Before leaving the premises, Yu ransacked the drawers and took out $4, 80 or 90 cents from the woman's handbag and a wrist watch from the body.

For six days he lay low in the western area. Believing that Yenping Road was in Chinese territory, Yu for several nights slept in unattended cars parked on the street. He pawned the watch and his clothes. He was arrested on Yenping Road on October 6 by Chinese Detective Constable 77.

Inquest Held
The verdict of the inquest on Miss Wexler by the court procurator was to the effect that death was caused by a blunt instrument and by suffocation. The boy has no previous convictions.

Those in charge of the case were Detective Sub-Inspector M. Crewther, Detective Sub-Inspector Chu Chi-huang and Detective-Sergeant S. Craig.

Question Of Burial
Miss Wexler was buried at the Hungjao Road cemetery, although the burial was at one time scheduled to be held at the Jewish cemetery on the ground that she was a Jewess. Her mother recently arrived from Harbin and is reported to have requested a re-burial at the Jewish cemetery. According to local Russians, Miss Wexler was formerly employed at the former Klienneman's Cafe and a local foreign hotel as a bar-girl. The murder of Miss Wexler drew city-wide interest, being the first murder of a foreigner by a Chinese this year.
page_data.zh:
韦克斯勒案凶手
被判终身监禁
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1938年10月19日
中国厨役获刑；被告
保持冷静

现年21岁的厨役余逸源（Yu Yih-yuen）因于9月30日在百老汇大厦谋杀22岁的俄国女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Wexler）小姐，今晨被第一特区地方法院王法官判处终身监禁。他也被终身剥夺公民权利。他将在提篮桥监狱服刑。

这名举止阴柔的年轻厨役平静地接受了判决。他今日未提出上诉通知，但预计他将向中国高等法院对判决提出上诉。

在警署辖区
这名来自浙江定海的年轻男子，于9月30日下午，在工部局警务处副总巡官H. M. 史密斯（H. M. Smyth）上尉的寓所内，因坏鸡蛋一事发生争吵后，杀害了韦克斯勒小姐。

这名厨役在案发六天后被捕时，无论是在警局还是在公开法庭上，都作了全面供认。该案仅经过两次庭审即告结案。

详情披露
在法庭上，被判罪的厨役以及市政检察官张唐尤（T. Y. Chang）先生均提供了关于罪行的详细情节。张先生在首次听证期间对他提出了预谋杀人指控。庭审中查明，余某自去年七月起受雇于史密斯上尉。

动机据称为报复
据称，实际杀人的动机是出于报复。他说，韦克斯勒小姐经常因他 alleged 懒散的习惯而责骂他，因此他与受害者关系不睦。案发当天，他因购买坏鸡蛋多次受到责骂，导致双方发生争吵，期间两人都采取了粗暴手段。他声称，他杀死她是因为害怕她会向史密斯上尉告发公寓内的打斗情况。

男孩与韦克斯勒小姐之间的争执发生在9月30日上午8点左右。他在为史密斯上尉和韦克斯勒小姐供应早餐时，因拿来坏鸡蛋而受到后者的斥责。他表示，当时他没有争辩。

购买鸡蛋
早餐后，史密斯上尉前往办公室上班，韦克斯勒小姐吩咐余某去市场买鸡蛋。上午10点左右，一位杰伊·杜科夫（Jay Dukoff）夫人拜访了韦克斯勒小姐。她们一同外出购买了一盒巧克力，韦克斯勒小姐在一小时内独自返回。

当余某正在打扫卧室时，据称韦克斯勒小姐再次责骂他没有从床下捡起脏丝绸内裤。就在此时，一名厨役的亲属打来电话。据称，韦克斯勒小姐又因他使用电话而生气。

发生打斗
韦克斯勒小姐跟着男孩来到厨房，她从窗台上拿起一个破损的鸡蛋，据称指责男孩买了坏鸡蛋。后者回嘴并从韦克斯勒小姐手中夺过鸡蛋。据称，她因此愤怒地打了男孩，男孩则用切肉刀的刀柄还击打她。

据称，韦克斯勒小姐威胁要将此事告诉史密斯上尉，并用俄语给一位朋友打电话。后来查明，韦克斯勒小姐是给杜科夫夫人打的电话。

随后她回到客厅阅读杂志。当时大约是12点30分。厨役再次被叫进去，这次据称是因没有 properly 擦拭桌子而受到责骂。此时，她的鼻子正在流血。

在地上搏斗
她突然注意到血迹，据称再次攻击男孩。两人在地上搏斗了一段时间，期间韦克斯勒小姐咬了男孩的手指并抓伤了他的脸，而她自己的手也被咬伤。较弱的一方韦克斯勒小姐停止了挣扎。

男孩回到厨房，从冰箱里拿出一整品脱瓶装的啤酒，再次走进客厅。他用酒瓶击打她的头部五六次。他穿过房间，拉下百叶窗。然后他拿出一大张吸墨纸，写了八个汉字，意思是：“害人不成反害己。”

拿走钱款和手表
就在这时，他听到那女人发出喘息声。惊慌之下，他找到一根帆布绳，系在她的脖子上。然后用一条毛巾和一条毯子盖住尸体。在离开现场前，余某翻查抽屉，从女人的手提包里拿走了4美元80或90美分，并从尸体上拿走了一块腕表。

他在西区躲藏了六天。余某认为延平路位于中国领土范围内，连续几晚睡在街上无人看管的汽车里。他典当了手表和衣服。10月6日，他在延平路被华捕77号侦探警员逮捕。

举行验尸审讯
法院检察官对韦克斯勒小姐死因的验尸裁决结论为：死因系钝器击打及窒息所致。该男孩此前无犯罪记录。

负责此案的人员包括：副探长M. Crewther、副探长朱志煌（Chu Chi-huang，音译）以及侦探警长S. Craig。

安葬问题
韦克斯勒小姐被安葬在虹桥路公墓，尽管曾一度计划将其安葬在犹太公墓，理由是她是犹太女性。她的母亲最近从哈尔滨抵达，据报道已请求改葬至犹太公墓。据当地俄国人称，韦克斯勒小姐以前曾在克利内曼咖啡馆（Klienneman's Cafe）和一家本地外资酒店担任酒吧女侍。韦克斯勒小姐被杀案引起了全市的关注，这是今年第一起中国人杀害外国人的案件。

October 15, 1938.

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

DEATH OF MARGARET WEXLER

At 2 p.m. September 30 a Russian lady named Margaret
Wexler living in Flat No.14 on the 5th floor of Broadway Mansions
was murdered by her house boy named Yu Yeh-yuen (俞逸源), age 21,
native of Ningpo. The murderer escaped but he was apprehended
several days later by Chinese detective sergeant Sung Kwei-hwa
(孫桂華) of West Hongkew Station in the vicinity of Connaught
Road and Yenping Road and subsequently handed over to Hongkew
Station. Together with Chow Ching-dong (周金生), a cook working
in the Mansions, who was a suspect in the case, he was arraigned
before the Shanghai First Special District Court and remanded in
custody. During the period of the remand, the Police ascertained
that Chow Ching-dong had no connection with the case and an
application was made for his release.

Yesterday the accused Yu Yeh-yuen appeared before the
Court. Mr. T.Y. Chang, Assistant Municipal Advocate, who
prosecuted, addressed the Court, saying "Some photographs have
been taken by the Police of the deceased after her death. It
has also been ascertained by the doctor that the wounds on the
deceased's head were caused by blunt or sharp instruments (photo-
graphs produced for the inspection of the Court). A wrist watch
worn by the deceased at the time of her death was stolen by the
accused who pledged it at the Cheng Dah Pawnshop (成大當鋪), No.909
Connaught Road, for $6. Now the watch cannot be recovered as the
accused sold the pawn ticket to a stranger who later redeemed it.
The accused is charged with manslaughter under Article 271,
Section 1, of the Chinese Criminal Code and in view of the
cruelty in which the accused committed the crime, the Court
is requested to impose the capital punishment."

Questioned by the Court, the accused stated that the
deceased caught hold of his hair, struck him and tore his coat
and he, in a fit of fury, struck back at her. He asked the
Court for leniency.

The Court ordered the accused to be remanded in
custody pending a judgment.

1938年10月15日。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

玛格丽特·韦克斯勒之死

9月30日下午2时，居住在百老汇大厦五楼14号公寓的一位名为玛格丽特·韦克斯勒的俄国女士，被其男仆余逸源（俞逸源），21岁，宁波人，谋杀。凶手逃逸，但数日后在康纳路（Connaught Road）和延平路附近，被北虹口捕房华捕探目孙桂華（Sung Kwei-hwa）抓获，随后移交虹口捕房。连同在大厦工作的厨师周金生（Chow Ching-dong，本案嫌疑人），他被提解至上海第一特区地方法院受审，并被还押候审。在还押期间，警方查明周金生与本案无关，遂申请将其释放。

昨日，被告余逸源出庭。助理市政检察官张唐尤（T.Y. Chang）先生作为控方发言，他对法庭说：“警方拍摄了死者死后的一些照片。医生也查明，死者头部的伤口是由钝器或利器造成的（照片已提交法庭查验）。死者遇害时佩戴的一块腕表被被告盗走，并在康纳路909号的成大當鋪以6美元的价格典当。现在手表无法追回，因为被告将当票卖给了一名陌生人，后者随后赎回了手表。被告被控违反《中华民国刑法》第271条第1款之杀人罪，鉴于被告作案手段残忍，请求法庭判处死刑。”

经法庭讯问，被告称死者抓住他的头发，殴打他并撕破他的外套，他在盛怒之下还击。他请求法庭从轻发落。

法庭命令被告还押候判。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

OCT 1 4 1938

Captain Smyth Talks In Secret
With Judge About Wexler Murder
Case; Cook-Boy Faces Tribunal
In Last Hearing; Judgment Due

Sentence Expected Wednesday
On Chinese Killer Of Young
Foreign Girl In Apartment

Smyth Dodges Open Court Testimony; Says Boy
Slack In Work, Gambled; Wexler Visitor
Identified; Boy Again Questioned

Says Victim Lived In Smyth Flat

Captain H. M. Smyth, O.B.E., deputy commissioner of the S.M.P., testified before Judge Wong in a half-hour secret session behind closed doors in the judges' private room at the First Special District Court this morning, in connection with the murder of Miss Margaret Wexler, 22-year-old Russian, who was killed by the officer's cook-boy, Yu Yih-yuen, 21, native of Tinghai, Ch'kiang, on September 30.

He is the only witness to testify before the court since the trial of the cook-boy started in the tribunal last week, following the boy's arrest on October 6 on Yen-ping Road. So far evidence was produced only by the municipal advocate, Mr. T. Y. Chang, and Detective Sub-Inspector M. Crowther, who was in charge of the case.

Secrecy Maintained

The testimony of Captain Smyth this morning was given on the top floor of the building, which is inaccessible to court attendants except judges and secretaries connected with the judicial organization. Great secrecy and mystery were attached to the session held between the judge and Captain Smyth, in the presence of the municipal advocate.

Captain Smyth arrived at the court shortly after 9 o'clock, and at about 9.30 o'clock he was escorted to the judges' recess room where the session took place behind closed doors. He left the court in his car at 10 o'clock.

Said Boy Was Slack

Both the advocate and the police officers in charge of the case were noncommittal in regard to the nature of the secret session, but it was learned from various sources that Captain Smyth gave information to the judge as to the character of his former cook-boy. He is understood to have said that the boy had been slack in his work lately and had been making frequent visits to gambling resorts.

The trial of the cook-boy was, however, held in the open court, soon after the conclusion of the private session. After a lengthy questioning of the accused and presentation of further evidence by Mr. Chang and Mr. Crowther, the judge called for a summing up of the case. Pleadings were concluded today and judgment was reserved until next Wednesday.

Photos Shown

Mr. Chang opened the session by presenting 10 photographs taken after the discovery of the murder victim in Apt. 14, Broadway Mansions, where the murder took place. The flat is occupied by Captain Smyth.

The pawnshop where the cook-boy pawned a wrist watch taken from Miss Wexler was located at 909 Connaught Road, according to the advocate. It was disclosed that the boy sold the pawn ticket to an unknown man, who redeemed the watch the following day. During the course of investigation, the police also recovered Captain Smyth's old clothes from a pawnshop. It is presumed that the boy stole the

1938年10月14日

史密斯上尉就韦克斯勒谋杀案
与法官秘密会谈；厨役面临
最后一次庭审；判决在即

预计周三宣判
杀害公寓内年轻外籍女子的
中国凶手刑期

史密斯回避公开法庭作证；称男孩工作
懒散、赌博；韦克斯勒的访客
身份确认；男孩再次受审

称受害者住在史密斯公寓

工部局警务处副总巡官H. M. 史密斯上尉（O.B.E.勋衔），今晨在第一特区地方法院法官私人房间内，就9月30日被该警官的厨役、21岁的浙江定海人余逸源杀害的22岁俄国女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒小姐谋杀案，在闭门举行的半小时秘密会议中向王法官作证。

自上周厨役受审以来，他是唯一在法庭作证的证人，该男孩于10月6日在延平路被捕。到目前为止，证据仅由市政检察官张唐尤（T. Y. Chang）先生和负责此案的副探长M. Crowther提供。

保密维持

史密斯上尉今晨的证词是在大楼顶层进行的，除法官和司法机构相关的秘书外，法庭工作人员不得进入。法官与史密斯上尉在市政检察官在场的情况下举行的会议，充满了高度的秘密和神秘色彩。

史密斯上尉在9点后不久到达法院，约9点30分，他被护送至法官休息室，会议在闭门状态下进行。他于10点乘车离开法院。

称男孩懒散

控方律师和负责此案的警官对秘密会议的性质均未置评，但从多方获悉，史密斯上尉向法官提供了关于其前任厨役品格的信息。据悉，他说该男孩最近工作懒散，并频繁光顾赌博场所。

然而，在私人会议结束后，厨役的审判随即在公开法庭举行。在对被告进行长时间讯问并由张先生和Crowther先生提交更多证据后，法官要求对案件进行总结陈述。辩论于今日结束，判决保留至下周三宣布。

展示照片

张先生开庭时展示了在谋杀案发生地——百老汇大厦14号公寓发现受害者后拍摄的10张照片。该公寓由史密斯上尉居住。

据检察官称，厨役典当从韦克斯勒小姐处偷来的腕表的当铺位于康纳路909号。披露显示，男孩将当票卖给了一名不明男子，该男子次日赎回了手表。在调查过程中，警方还从一家当铺追回了史密斯上尉的旧衣服。据推测，男孩偷窃了

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

OCT 1 4 1938

clothes and pawned them, according to the attorney.

Had Visitor

The Russian woman who called on Miss Wexler on the morning of the day of the murder was Mrs. Iay Dukoff, who lives at Apt 101 Majestic Apartments, Bubbling Well Road. She is reported to have told the police that she went to Broadway Mansions at about 10 o'clock that morning and both went out to buy a box of chocolates. Miss Wexler returned to the flat within 40 minutes. It was Mrs. Dukoff who received a telephone message from Miss Wexler shortly after noon, but nothing was said about the altercation between Miss Wexler and the boy, it was stated. Mrs. Dukoff was not in court today to testify. The advocate also told the court that the hair found on the beer bottle was that of the victim, as a result of examination by chemists.

The cook-boy was then questioned by the judge.
"When did you start working for Captain Smyth?" asked the judge.
Cook: "Some time in July last year."

Girl Lived There

Judge. "When you became a cook in his (Captain Smyth's) employ in July last year, was Miss Wexler living in the flat?"
Cook: "Yes. I found her living there."

The cook-boy then recounted what he had said during the previous hearing last week, saying that he was scolded often by Miss Wexler. He admitted that his brother-in-law, who was formerly a cook-boy in the employ of Captain Smyth, had warned him on September 20 that his master was planning to find another cook because of his alleged slack habits. Yu admitted that he slept late in the morning several times and was accordingly scolded for it.

Changes Testimony

The cook-boy practically reiterated the same statement he made during the last hearing, with one exception. Refuting his former confession, he denied that he took out a small beer bottle (Horsehead brand) from the refrigerator and struck her with it five or six times. He said that the bottle was taken out of the refrigerator by Miss Wexler.

The advocate then explained that Miss Wexler, according to investigations, was a total abstainer and she therefore would not have taken out the bottle.

Mr. Crowther testified that the refrigerator had ample room for the beer bottle and there was no reason why it should have been taken out by the victim. To this the boy had nothing to say.

Writes Characters

The boy was asked to re-write the eight characters he had written on a big piece of blotting paper, which read, "If you do not succeed in injuring others, you will injure yourself." The handwriting was similar beyond a doubt declared the judge after reading the duplicate copy. The boy was questioned no further.

Mr. Chang, in summing up the case, stated that evidence tends to show that the murder had been premeditated. The fact that the boy struck the woman with the beer bottle after she ceased to struggle and that he tied a string around her neck and smothered her with a blanket is proof that the murder was deliberate, the advocate continued. There was no question of self-defense as the woman was unconscious when the boy struck her with the bottle, the attorney concluded. He asked the judge to mete out a severe punishment to the cook-boy, in spite of the fact that he has no previous convictions.

Asks Leniency

Mr. Pao Ching, attorney then took the stand and defended the accused. He asked leniency on the ground that the boy had no criminal record and that he committed the crime in a fit of rage.

The murder of Miss Wexler, which is drawing close attention in Shanghai despite high police efforts to hush it up, took place between 1 and 3 o'clock on the afternoon of September 30 in Captain Smyth's flat. The boy, who has not been on friendly terms with the victim, was scolded during breakfast by Miss Wexler, for serving bad eggs.

Got Into Fight

Nothing happened until noon when Miss Wexler again allegedly scolded the boy for having purchased a damaged egg which she found on the window sill in the kitchen. She allegedly slapped the boy. They quarreled and both resorted to rough-house tactics during which the boy struck her with the handle of a knife.

Shortly afterward, they resumed their quarrel in the living room. They struggled on the floor for some time. When the woman ceased to struggle, the boy took out a bottle of beer from the refrigerator and struck her several times with it. Then he tied a piece of string around her neck and smothered her with a blanket. After writing the eight Chinese characters, he changed his clothes and escaped to the western district, where he was located six days later.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1938年10月14日

据律师称，（被告）将衣物典当。

有访客

谋杀案发生当天上午拜访韦克斯勒小姐（Miss Wexler）的俄国女子是艾·杜科夫夫人（Mrs. Iay Dukoff），她住在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）美琪公寓（Majestic Apartments）101室。据报她告诉警方，那天上午约10点钟她去了百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions），随后两人一起出去买了一盒巧克力。韦克斯勒小姐在40分钟内回到了公寓。据说，中午过后不久，是杜科夫夫人接到了韦克斯勒小姐的电话留言，但并未提及韦克斯勒小姐与那名男童之间的争执。杜科夫夫人今天未出庭作证。辩护律师还告诉法庭，经化学家检验，在啤酒瓶上发现的头发属于受害者。

法官随后讯问了厨童。
法官问：“你什么时候开始为史密斯上尉（Captain Smyth）工作的？”
厨童答：“去年七月的某个时候。”

女孩曾住在那里

法官问：“去年七月你成为他（史密斯上尉）雇用的厨师时，韦克斯勒小姐是否住在那套公寓里？”
厨童答：“是的。我发现她住在那里。”

随后，这名厨童复述了上周上次听证会上的证词，称他经常受到韦克斯勒小姐的责骂。他承认，他的姐夫（以前也是史密斯上尉雇用的厨童）曾在9月20日警告他，说主人因为他 allegedly 懒散的习惯正打算另找一名厨师。余（Yu）承认他早上几次睡懒觉，并因此受到责骂。

改变证词

除了一个例外，这名厨童几乎重申了他在上次听证会上所做的相同陈述。他否认了之前的供认，辩称并非他从冰箱里拿出一小瓶啤酒（马头牌），并用它击打她五六次。他说瓶子是韦克斯勒小姐从冰箱里拿出来的。

辩护律师随后解释说，据调查，韦克斯勒小姐是完全禁酒者，因此她不会拿出那瓶酒。

克劳瑟先生（Mr. Crowther）作证说，冰箱里有足够的空间放那瓶啤酒，没有理由由受害者将其取出。对此，该男童无话可说。

书写汉字

法官要求该男童重新书写他之前写在一大张吸墨纸上的八个汉字，内容是：“害人不成反害己”。法官在阅读副本后宣布，笔迹无疑相似。不再对该男童进行进一步讯问。

张先生在总结案情时指出，证据倾向于表明这起谋杀是有预谋的。辩护律师继续说道，事实是该男童在女子停止挣扎后用啤酒瓶击打她，并在她脖子上系了一根绳子，用毯子闷死她，这证明谋杀是故意的。律师总结道，由于该男童用瓶子击打女子时她已失去知觉，因此不存在自卫的问题。尽管该厨童无前科，他仍请求法官对其处以严厉惩罚。

请求宽恕

随后，律师鲍靖先生（Mr. Pao Ching）出庭为被告辩护。他以该男童无犯罪记录且是在盛怒之下犯罪为由，请求从轻发落。

尽管警方极力掩盖，韦克斯勒小姐被杀案在上海引起了广泛关注，该案发生于9月30日下午1点至3点之间，地点在史密斯上尉的公寓内。这名与受害者关系不和的男童在早餐时因端上坏鸡蛋而遭到韦克斯勒小姐的责骂。

发生斗殴

直到中午才发生变故，当时韦克斯勒小姐 allegedly 再次因男童买了一个破损的鸡蛋而责骂他，该鸡蛋是她发现放在厨房窗台上的。她 allegedly 打了男童一巴掌。他们争吵起来，双方在扭打中，男童用刀柄击打了她。

不久之后，他们在客厅继续争吵。他们在地板上搏斗了一段时间。当女子停止挣扎时，男童从冰箱里拿出一瓶啤酒，用它击打她数次。然后他在她脖子上系了一根绳子，并用毯子闷死她。写下那八个汉字后，他换了衣服逃往西区，六天后在那里被找到。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 1 1 1938

Mother Wants
Re-Burial Of
Veksler Body

Claims Daughter Was Of
Jewish Faith, Rates
Second Funeral

It was learned yesterday by THE
CHINA PRESS that Mrs. R. Mordoho-
vich, the mother of the late
Margaret Veksler who arrived in
Shanghai last week from Dairen,
has already approached officials in
charge of the Jewish cemetery here
to have her daughter re-buried in
the Baikal Road cemetery.

It was stated by a leading official
of the Jewish community here that
this measure was being insisted
upon by Mrs. Mordohovich, who
claimed that her daughter belong-
ed to the Jewish faith and, there-
fore, should be accorded rites ac-
cording to her religion.

The official maintained, however,
that the transfer arrangements
would be discussed immediately fol-
lowing the Jewish festival of Suc-
coth which is now in progress.

Margaret Veksler was buried in
the Hungjao Cemetery on October
2 following her tragic death in a
flat in the Broadway Mansions two
days earlier.

Indications were made to THE
CHINA PRESS by the Jewish official
that on his own instance he had
approached the police in order to
receive the body of the girl for her
burial at the Jewish Cemetery on
Baikal Road.

However, the official stated,
despite giving the police proof of
the deceased girl's religious belief,
the burial was carried out at the
Hungjao Cemetery under different
religious principles.

1938年10月11日

母亲希望
重新安葬
韦克斯勒遗体

声称女儿信奉
犹太教，要求
举行第二次葬礼

本报昨日获悉，已故玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Veksler）的母亲R·莫尔多霍维奇夫人（Mrs. R. Mordohovich）上周从大连抵达上海后，已联系此处负责犹太公墓的官员，要求将其女儿重新安葬在倍开尔路（Baikal Road）公墓。

此处犹太社区的一位主要官员表示，莫尔多霍维奇夫人坚持要求采取这一措施，她声称其女儿属于犹太教信徒，因此应按照其宗教仪式办理丧事。

然而，该官员坚持认为，转移遗体的安排将在目前正在进行的犹太住棚节（Succoth）结束后立即讨论。

玛格丽特·韦克斯勒于两天前在百老汇大厦的一套公寓内悲惨身亡后，于10月2日被安葬在虹桥公墓。

这位犹太官员向本报暗示，是他主动联系警方，以便接收该女孩的遗体，将其安葬在倍开尔路的犹太公墓。

然而，该官员表示，尽管已向警方提供证据证明该已故女孩的宗教信仰，但葬礼却是按照不同的宗教原则在虹桥公墓举行的。

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

THE MURDER IN BROADWAY MANSIONS

At about 1 p.m. September 30, a Russian lady named Margaret Wexler, age 22, was murdered at her home, Room No.14 on the 5th floor of Broadway Mansions. Officers from Hongkew Police Station ascertained that one Chow Ching-dong (周金東), native of Ningpo, a boy employed to look after Room 514 of the Mansions, was concerned in the murder.

Chow was arrested and charged in Court where he made a statement that the crime was committed by Yu Yeh-yuen (俞逸源), also of Ningpo, age 21, a boy working in Room No.14. Sung Kwei-hwa (宋桂華) of West Hongkew Police Station received information that Yu Yeh-yuen had been seen in the vicinity of Yenping Road, Zau Ka Tu (曹家渡). Yesterday morning Yu Yeh-yuen was arraigned before the First Shanghai Special District Court.

Boy Admits Killing Miss
Veksler After Quarrel

Resented Steady Nagging By Russian Girl Over
Purchase Of Eggs And Alleged Failure To
Clean Apartment; Describes Struggle

SHANGHAI TIMES.    Standing calmly in the dock in a crowded courtroom at the First Special District Court yesterday morning, Yu Yen-yuen, 20-year-old cook-boy formerly employed by Captain H. M. Smyth, o.B.E., Deputy Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, pleaded guilty to the charge of having murdered Miss Margaret Veksler, 22-year-old Russian-Jewess.

In a few words Yu, a small, effeminate-looking native of Tinghai, who was arrested on Thursday afternoon on Yenping Road by S.M.P., detectives, described his motive for the terrible crime. "I killed her because of a couple of eggs," he said, "she thought I bought bad eggs and scolded me for it! We quarrelled, fought, and in the end I suppose I killed her."

Almost at the start of the hearing Yu pleaded guilty to the charge of murder which was brought against him by the Assistant Municipal Advocate, Mr. T. Y. Chang. The advocate then immediately commenced outlining the case for the prosecution, based on police findings and the confession which had been made by Yu at the Hongkew Police Station shortly after his arrest. After Mr. Chang had concluded his lengthy outline of the case, Yu was questioned by Judge Wong and described in detail the events that transpired in Captain Smyth's apartment at the Broadway Mansions on the day of the murder, Friday, September 30.

**Scolded Boy**

Evidence given during the hearing tended to show that the murdered woman had repeatedly scolded the boy for alleged laxity in his duties. Yu, who had been in the employ of Captain Smyth, since July, 1937, was for some time on bad terms with Miss Veksler. His salary it was stated was $20 per month.

On the day of the murder, the advocate told the court, Yu as usual got up early to attend to his duties in Captain Smyth's apartment. At 8 a.m. he served breakfast to Captain Smyth and Miss Veksler. When he served the eggs, Miss Veksler scolded him, saying that the eggs were bad. He felt "peeved" but did not argue, the advocate continued. At 8.15 a.m. Captain Smyth left for the office and about an hour later Miss Veksler asked the boy to buy four eggs at the market giving him $5. He went to the market and bought two ducks eggs and two chicken eggs. Upon returning he gave Miss Veksler $4.60 change. Later in the morning a Russian woman friend of Miss Veksler arrived and Yu left the apartment for a few minutes to change his clothes.

**Objects to Phone Call**

At about noon as Yu was cleaning up in the bedroom, he was approached by the deceased and again allegedly scolded for not having cleaned the room properly. She allegedly picked up some clothing from under the bed and appeared to be angry because the boy had not put it away. Just then a telephone rang and when Miss Veksler answered it, it was for the boy, she later scolded him for having people call him at the apartment.

The boy went back to the kitchen and picked up a big black handled meat knife, the advocate declared. Miss Veksler then came into the kitchen and seeing a broken egg on the window sill, scolded the boy saying that he always had bought bad eggs. The boy snatched the egg away and replied that he had bought the egg for himself. This allegedly infuriated Miss Veksler and she slapped the boy. He struck back and hit her once on the nose with the handle of the knife. She then pulled his ears and dragged him into the drawing room. The boy broke loose and Miss Veksler telephoned someone in Russian. Then she sat down to read a magazine.

**Death Struggle**

A little later Miss Veksler again called the boy and scolded him for having failed to dust the table. At the time she noticed that blood was trickling out of her nose, and allegedly angered made an attack on the boy. A struggle ensued and they fell on the floor, during which she bit his third finger and scratched his face. The boy gave her five or six heavy blows on the face and bit her left palm. He also butted her face with his head. Apparently weakened, Miss Veksler ceased to struggle.

The prosecutor, at this stage, informed the judge that it was at that time that the boy stated that he had decided to kill the woman, as he was afraid that she would tell Captain Smyth of the day's happenings. He then took out a small full bottle of Horsehead brand beer from the refrigerator and struck her on the forehead five or six times. He also pulled down the blind in the room.

**Wrote Philosophy**

Apparently being a bit of a philosopher, Yu picked up a big piece of blotting paper and wrote in Chinese characters, "If you do not succeed in injuring others, you will injure yourself." While he was writing, he heard the woman gasp. Determined to do away with her, he got a strip of canvas string and tied it tightly around her neck and put a towel over her head and then covered her body with a blanket. Before he left the apartment he ransacked the drawer and found $4, and took 80 or 90 cents from the victim's bag, and her wrist watch on her left arm. When he left at about 1.30 p.m. he met the floor boy, who asked him with whom he had been fighting.

After leaving the apartment Yu slept for six nights in alleyways off Yenping Road. He pawned the watch for $7, and lost $8 in gambling.

**Admits Everything**

Yu admitted everything the advocate outlined to the court, but stated that the murder was not premeditated. He said he thought of killing her when he found her unconscious. He could not tell whether she was actually killed by the blows inflicted with the beer bottle or by strangulation. Yu stated that the deceased had often scolded him and wanted Captain Smyth to get a new boy.

The judge's attention was called to Yu's bitten finger and the injured left hand of the victim, indicating that the confession corresponded in many details with the police findings. The floor boy, Chu Chin-dong, who was arrested last Sunday, was ordered to be detained by the court, together with Yu until next Friday.

少年承认争吵后杀害维克斯勒小姐

怨恨俄国女子因购买鸡蛋及 alleged 未打扫公寓而不断唠叨；描述搏斗过程

《上海泰晤士报》。昨日上午，在第一特区法院拥挤的法庭上，前上海公共租界工部局警务处副总监 H. M. Smyth 上尉（O.B.E.勋衔）雇用的20岁厨役俞逸源（Yu Yen-yuen）平静地站在被告席上，对谋杀22岁俄籍犹太女子玛格丽特·维克斯勒（Margaret Veksler）小姐的指控认罪。

俞某身材瘦小，相貌阴柔，系定海人。他在周四下午于延平路被工部局警务处侦探逮捕。他用寥寥数语描述了犯下这桩可怕罪行的动机。“我杀她是因为几个鸡蛋，”他说，“她以为我买了坏鸡蛋，为此责骂我！我们争吵、打斗，最后我想是我杀了她。”

听证会刚开始，俞某即对助理市政检察官张唐氏（T. Y. Chang）先生提出的谋杀指控表示认罪。随后，检察官立即开始概述控方案情，依据是警方的调查结果以及俞某被捕后不久在虹口巡捕房所作的供认。在张先生 lengthy 地概述完案情后，王法官对俞某进行了讯问，俞某详细描述了案发当日（9月30日，星期五）在百老汇大厦 Smyth 上尉公寓内发生的事件。

**责骂少年**

听证期间提供的证据显示，被害女子曾多次责骂该少年，称其工作懈怠。俞某自1937年7月起受雇于 Smyth 上尉，有一段时间与维克斯勒小姐关系不和。据称，他的月薪为20元。

检察官告诉法庭，案发当日，俞某像往常一样早起，在 Smyth 上尉的公寓里履行职责。上午8点，他为 Smyth 上尉和维克斯勒小姐送上早餐。当他端上鸡蛋时，维克斯勒小姐责骂他，说鸡蛋坏了。检察官继续说道，他感到“恼火”，但没有争辩。上午8点15分，Smyth 上尉前往办公室上班，约一小时后，维克斯勒小姐让少年去市场买四个鸡蛋，给了他5元钱。他去市场买了两个鸭蛋和两个鸡蛋。回来后，他找给维克斯勒小姐4元6角零钱。上午晚些时候，维克斯勒小姐的一位俄国女性朋友到来，俞某离开公寓几分钟去换衣服。

**反对打电话**

中午时分，俞某正在卧室打扫卫生，死者走近他，再次 allegedly 责骂他没有把房间打扫干净。据称，她从床底下捡起一些衣物，似乎因为少年没有收拾好而生气。就在这时，电话铃响了，维克斯勒小姐接听后发现是找少年的，随后她责骂少年让人往公寓里给他打电话。

检察官宣称，少年回到厨房，拿起一把黑色大柄切肉刀。随后维克斯勒小姐走进厨房，看到窗台上有一个破鸡蛋，便责骂少年，说他总是买坏鸡蛋。少年抢过鸡蛋，回答说那是他为自己买的。这 allegedly 激怒了维克斯勒小姐，她打了少年一巴掌。他还手，用刀柄击打她的鼻子一下。随后她揪住他的耳朵，将他拖进客厅。少年挣脱开来，维克斯勒小姐用俄语给某人打了电话。然后她坐下阅读杂志。

**致死搏斗**

过了一会儿，维克斯勒小姐再次叫来少年，责骂他没有掸桌子上的灰尘。当时她注意到血正从鼻子里流出来，据称因愤怒而攻击少年。随即发生搏斗，两人倒在地上，期间她咬了他的第三根手指，抓伤了他的脸。少年朝她脸上重击五六下，并咬了她的左手掌。他还用头撞她的脸。维克斯勒小姐显然力气耗尽，停止了挣扎。

在此阶段，检察官告知法官，就在那时，少年声称他决定杀死这名女子，因为他害怕她会向 Smyth 上尉告发当天发生的事情。随后，他从冰箱里拿出一瓶满装的马头牌（Horsehead）小瓶啤酒，朝她的前额击打五六次。他还拉下了房间里的百叶窗。

**写下哲理**

俞某似乎有点哲学家的气质，他拿起一大张吸墨纸，用汉字写道：“害人不成反害己。”当他书写时，听到那女子发出喘息声。决心除掉她后，他找来一条帆布带子，紧紧勒住她的脖子，用毛巾盖住她的头，然后用毯子盖住她的身体。在离开公寓前，他翻查抽屉，找到4元钱，并从受害者的包里拿走80或90分钱，以及她左臂上的手表。他在下午1点30分左右离开时，遇到了楼层侍者，后者问他刚才在和谁打架。

离开公寓后，俞某在延平路附近的小巷里睡了六晚。他将手表典当得7元，并在赌博中输掉8元。

**承认一切**

俞某承认了检察官向法庭概述的所有情节，但声称谋杀并非预谋。他说，当他发现她不省人事时才想到要杀她。他无法确定她是死于啤酒瓶的击打还是被勒死。俞某称，死者经常责骂他，并希望 Smyth 上尉换个新仆人。

法官注意到俞某被咬伤的手指和受害者受伤的左手，这表明供词在许多细节上与警方调查结果相符。上周日被捕的楼层侍者朱金堂（Chu Chin-dong，音译）被法庭命令与俞某一同羁押，直至下周五。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

OCT 7 1938

“Boy” Confesses to
Woman’s Murder

Settlement Police Arrest
Criminal Six Days After
Brutal Hongkew Slaying

The frail, almost girlish, cook-boy suspected of the brutal murder, on September 30, of Miss Margaret Wexler (or Vexler) in a flat at the Broadway Mansions, was arrested at 3.30 p.m. yesterday in the Zaokadoo village, near Jessfield, where he had apparently been hiding ever since the crime, living from hand to mouth on $4—his only resources when he fled—and sleeping in casual places where he thought he would not be noticed by the regular residents.

The cook-boy, Yu Yeh-yuen, 19-year-old native of Tinghai in the Chusan Islands of Chekiang Province, was arrested by detectives attached to “C” Division in which the murder took place. He was picked up on a tip supplied to the Settlement Police as a result of the exhaustive investigation conducted by the authorities throughout Shanghai since the murder. He readily confessed that he killed the young woman and then fled with the utmost despatch.

Miss Wexler, 22-year-old Russian, was murdered in the Broadway Mansions flat between 12.30 and 1.15 p.m. on September 30, according to Yu’s confession. He killed her, he said, in a fit of anger induced by a quarrel over some trivial domestic matter. Death was caused by the young servant picking up a small beer bottle and striking Miss Wexler with it on the head several times, causing deep wounds in the forehead and left temple and a heavy loss of blood. The body was not discovered until more than five hours later, when the murderer had already made his escape. It is believed that he went to Zaokadoo almost direct, using his Japanese pass to cross the Soochow Creek. He made no attempt, apparently, to leave Shanghai for his native province.

“Boy” Admits Quarrel

Yu frankly admitted yesterday that he had had a quarrel with Miss Wexler immediately before he killed her, and disposed of the early theory that robbery was the motive for the crime.

The arrest of the missing cook-boy brought relief to the staff of detectives who had been working day and night on the case since last Friday. The prisoner was taken immediately to Hongkew Police Station, where he was questioned at length for several hours. It was understood that he was taken last night to the scene of the crime, on the fifth floor of the Broadway Mansions, for a sort of reconstruction of the gruesome event. He was returned to the Hongkew Station last night and will be brought before the First Special District Court this morning. It is expected that the police will ask for a remand in order to enable them to continue their enquiry before they present the case.

Floor-Coolie Questioned

Yu’s arrest was the second one made since the murder. On October 2 a floor coolie at the Broadway Mansions was detained when a pair of blood-stained trousers found in the apartment where Miss Wexler was murdered, were identified as his. He explained that the trousers had been borrowed from him by Yu, a contention that was confirmed by last night’s findings.

He was held by the First Special District Court pending further inquiries. At the time of his arrest also he was considered to have been only indirectly concerned, as a close friend of the absconded Yu.

《字林西报》，

1938年10月7日

“少年”供认杀害妇女

凶残虹口杀人案六日后，租界警方逮捕罪犯

这名涉嫌于9月30日在百老汇大厦公寓内残忍谋杀玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Wexler，或拼作 Vexler）小姐的瘦弱、几乎带有女孩气的厨役，于昨日下午3点30分在兆丰公园附近的赵家渡村（Zaokadoo village，音译）被捕。自犯罪以来，他显然一直藏匿于此，靠逃亡时仅有的4元钱维持生计，睡在他认为不会被常住居民注意到的临时场所。

这名厨役名叫俞叶元（Yu Yeh-yuen，音译），19岁，浙江省舟山群岛定海人，由发生谋杀案的“C”区侦缉队侦探逮捕。他是根据当局自谋杀案发生后在整个上海进行的详尽调查所获得的线索而被工部局警务处抓获的。他坦率承认杀害了这名年轻女子，随后迅速逃窜。

根据俞某的供认，22岁的俄国人韦克斯勒小姐于9月30日中午12点30分至1点15分之间在百老汇大厦的公寓内被杀。他说，他是因一些琐碎的家事争吵引发的愤怒冲动下杀死了她。死因是这名年轻仆人拿起一个小啤酒瓶，多次击打韦克斯勒小姐的头部，造成前额和左太阳穴深伤口及大量失血。直到五个多小时后凶手已经逃脱，尸体才被发现。据信，他使用日本通行证越过苏州河，几乎直接前往赵家渡。显然，他并未试图离开上海返回原籍省份。

**“少年”承认争吵**

俞某昨日坦承，在杀害韦克斯勒小姐之前不久曾与她发生过争吵，从而排除了早期关于抢劫是犯罪动机的理论。

失踪厨役的被捕让自上周五以来日夜奋战在此案上的侦探团队松了一口气。囚犯立即被带往虹口巡捕房，在那里接受了数小时的详细讯问。据悉，昨晚他被带到百老汇大厦五楼的案发现场，对这一恐怖事件进行了某种程度的重建。昨晚他被送回虹口巡捕房，并将于今天上午被提审至第一特区法院。预计警方将要求还押候审，以便在提交案件前继续调查。

**讯问楼层苦力**

俞某的被捕是自谋杀案以来的第二次逮捕。10月2日，百老汇大厦的一名楼层苦力被拘留，因为在维克斯勒小姐被杀的公寓里发现的一条沾血长裤被确认为他的。他解释说，这条裤子是俞某向他借的，这一说法得到了昨晚调查结果证实。

第一特区法院将其扣留以待进一步调查。在被捕时，他也被认为仅间接涉案，因为是潜逃者俞某的密友。

M. WEKSLER 谋杀谜案仍未侦破。

死因研讯闭门举行。

公共租界工部局警务处昨日继续搜捕一名名为 Yu Yueh-yuen（俞月元，音译）的20岁中国男子，该男子籍贯宁波，涉嫌谋杀21岁的 Margaret Weksler-Kaimovich。死者于前天在上海公共租界工部局副总监 J.M. Smythe 上尉所寓居的公寓内被发现身亡。

警方昨日仍认为，这起谋杀案系该少年所为，其动机显然是为了抢劫这名年轻女子的财物。

昨日在殓房举行的死因研讯为闭门进行。这一情况更增添了围绕此谋杀案的神秘气氛。

警方拒绝透露有关罪行的任何细节，甚至不愿提供死因研讯结果及检察官裁决的简要说明。

从发生谋杀案的房间的整体状况来看，Weksler 小姐似乎进行了反抗。家具被移离原位或翻倒，以及受害者的衣服被撕破，这些事实都表明了这一点。

在殓房。

上午10时左右，大量参与调查此案的警务官员聚集在胶州路与延平路路口的公共殓房。

死者遗体停放在殓房的一个独立区域，覆盖着一块棕色布料。这位年轻女子美丽的面容已遭毁损，几乎无法辨认。双眼半闭。面部因头部左侧的伤口而血迹斑斑。

She was dressed in a simple blue coloured summer dress.

At 10 a.m. sharp, Captain G.M. Smythe accompanied by two detectives arrived to give evidence.

At 11 a.m. arrived Mr. Kuo Wei, Procurator of the 1st Special District Court, accompanied by his staff and Dr. Wei Li Kung. The Procurator and doctor examined the body of the young woman.

Held in camera

Immediately after the Procurator had occupied his place in the court room, a Sub-Inspector of the uniform branch of the S.M.P., cleared the room from public and newspapermen, stating that in accordance with instructions from high police authorities, the inquest would be held "in camera".

However, the doors of the room remained open ,and newspaper-men could see all that was going on in it.

For about 10 minutes a Sub-Inspector of the S.M.P. outlined to the court the details of police investigations. He was followed by the detective on duty who demonstrated before the Procurator various exhibits relating to the crime, including the blanket in which the victim's head had been wrapped after the murder, the empty beer bottle with which the fatal blow had been struck etc.

Then evidence was given by Captain G.M. Smythe, in whose apartment this bestial murder had taken place. He was followed by Dr. Wei Li Kung who reported on the result of his examination of the body. Captain Smythe was recalled, after which evidence was given by two detectives and two Chinese employees of the Broadway Mansion. Captain Smythe was again recalled as well as the detectives.

During the court proceedings a large group of the deceased's friends and acquaintances arrived to the mortuary. They were refused admittance to the court room. A Sergeant on duty also did not allow them to see the body of Margaret Weksler.

The inquest took quite a long time, instead of the usual 10-15 minutes.

上午10时整，G.M. Smythe 上尉在两名侦探的陪同下抵达作证。

上午11时，第一特区地方法院检察官郭伟（Kuo Wei，音译）先生在其职员及魏立功（Wei Li Kung，音译）医生的陪同下抵达。检察官和医生检查了这位年轻女子的遗体。

闭门举行

检察官刚在法庭就座，一名上海公共租界工部局警务处制服部的副督察便清退了公众和报界人士，声称根据警方高层的指示，死因研讯将“闭门”进行。

然而，房间的门一直敞开着，报界人士可以看到里面发生的一切。

上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名副督察向法庭概述了警方调查的细节，历时约10分钟。随后，值班侦探向检察官展示了与犯罪有关的各种证物，包括谋杀后包裹受害者头部的毯子、用于实施致命打击的空啤酒瓶等。

接着，谋杀案发生地公寓的住户 G.M. Smythe 上尉提供了证词。随后，魏立功（Wei Li Kung，音译）医生报告了他对遗体检查的结果。Smythe 上尉再次被传唤作证，之后两名侦探和百老汇大厦的两名中国雇员提供了证词。Smythe 上尉及侦探们再次被传唤。

在法庭诉讼期间，一大群死者的朋友和熟人来到殓房。他们被拒绝进入法庭。值班警长也不允许他们瞻仰 Margaret Weksler 的遗体。

死因研讯持续了相当长的时间，而非通常的10至15分钟。

Immediately upon the conclusion of the inquest Captain
Smythe and the detectives departed.

Who is Margaret Weksler?

Margaret Weksler was well known in this city and during the
five years of her residence here acquired a large number of
friends and acquaintances. The sudden death of the young woman
was a great blow to them.

Margaret Weksler was born in Russia. She lost her father
when she was still a child. She was 10 years of age when she ar-
rived in Harbin together with her mother. In Harbin her mother
married a certain Mordohovich, She is still residing in that city
and a telegram was sent yesterday notifying her of the sudden death
of her daughter.

Towards the end of 1932 Margaret Weksler married one Alfred
Albert Haimovich. Together with her husband she returned to Shang-
hai. However, they did not stay here long and soon left for Hankow
from where they subsequently proceeded to Nanking.

They returned here in the beginning of 1934.

Their married life proved to be unhappy and soon afterwards
the couple were divorced.

Margaret Weksler then obtained a position. At first she
worked in the "Little Chocolate Shop" and the" Chocolate Shop"
owned by A.S. Kleinermann. About two years ago she obtained a posi-
tion in the "Metropole Hotel" bar where, being on duty, she made
her acquaintance with Captain G.M. Smythe.

There can be no question of robbery.

"She never had much money or valuables" ,told us a close
friend of the late Margaret Weksler. - " She wore a small , unexpensive ring and a wrist watch. But even these articles she did not wear
lately as, according to what she told me herself, she had been com-
pelled to pawn these articles. There can be no question of rob-
bery as a motive of the murder!"

" Some time ago it was decided that Margaret would go to
England to reside there permanently. At first she intended to

死因研讯一结束，Smythe 上尉和侦探们便离开了。

谁是 Margaret Weksler？

Margaret Weksler 在本市广为人知，在她居住的五年间，结识了大量的朋友和熟人。这位年轻女子的突然离世对他们来说是一个巨大的打击。

Margaret Weksler 出生于俄罗斯。她在孩童时期便失去了父亲。10岁时，她与母亲一同抵达哈尔滨。在哈尔滨，她的母亲嫁给了一个名叫 Mordohovich 的人。她母亲至今仍居住在该市，昨日已向其发送电报，通知其女儿突然去世的消息。

1932年底，Margaret Weksler 嫁给了 Alfred Albert Haimovich。她与丈夫一同返回上海。然而，他们在此并未久留，不久便前往汉口，随后又从那里去了南京。

他们于1934年初回到这里。

他们的婚姻生活并不幸福，不久后两人便离婚了。

随后，Margaret Weksler 找到了一份工作。起初，她在 A.S. Kleinermann 拥有的“小巧克力店”（Little Chocolate Shop）和“巧克力店”（Chocolate Shop）工作。大约两年前，她在“大都会酒店”（Metropole Hotel）酒吧找到了一份工作，正是在那里值班时，她结识了 G.M. Smythe 上尉。

抢劫之说不能成立。

“前一段时间，大家决定让 Margaret 去英国永久居住。起初她打算

stay with Captain Smythe's parents and then to try to get in a

settled and she would be leaving Shanghai in two-three months

making the necessary shopping etc. She looked forward with plea-

The deceased was a person of exceptional qualities. Her

I often visited her in her apartment at the Broadway Man-

住在 Smythe 上尉的父母家，然后试着找份工作。

她去英国的问题已最终确定，她将在两三个月内离开上海。最近，Margaret 忙于为旅行做准备，购买必需品等。她对预期的旅程充满期待。

死者是一位品质卓越的人。她的一生充满了悲伤和失望。她非常善良、富有同情心且敏感，深受所有认识她的人的爱戴和友谊。

我经常去她在百老汇大厦的公寓看望她。我们常在那里打麻将，然后一起去看电影。

最近，她变得开朗快乐。她极其漂亮，虽然我手头这张业余拍摄的照片未能完全展现她的美貌，但即使在这张照片上，她看起来也是个美丽的孩子。

她的悲剧性死亡对所有认识并爱戴她的人来说都是一个巨大的打击”，Weksler 小姐的朋友结束了她的讲述。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 5 1938

Wants Information

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS
Sir,—We have heard of a law for the rich and a law for the poor, but in Shanghai, apparently, there exists a law exclusively for the great, as illustrated by the current inquiry into the tragic murder of a young woman in the apartment of a highly-placed police official.
It is far from my intention to suggest that the morbid curiosity of the public be satisfied with an orgy of gruesome detail regarding the poor woman's death but I would like to ask whether the inquiry is being held in camera (a) simply because it involves a police official; or (b) because publication of details might raise such a scandal that ratepayers would demand a civic investigation.
If the case is being held in camera for either of these two reasons, then there has been a clear betrayal of trust towards the ratepayers and the matter should be taken up immediately by the responsible authorities. It is inconceivable that there should be anything to hide from the public if there has been murder pure and simple; in fact, for its own protection, the public should be made acquainted with the essential facts.
May I express the earnest hope that this curious reticence by the police and press will cease immediately, and thereby put an end to the wild speculation now going on over the tragedy. Yours, etc.,
JUSTICE.
Shanghai, October 4, 1938

要求提供信息

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——我们听说过富人有富人的法律，穷人有穷人的法律，但在上海，显然存在一种专为权贵制定的法律，目前对一位高级警务官员公寓内发生的年轻女子悲惨谋杀案的调查便是例证。
我绝非意图建议以关于这位可怜女子死亡的恐怖细节盛宴来满足公众的病态好奇心，但我想知道，此次调查闭门进行是因为（a）仅仅涉及一名警务官员；还是（b）因为公布细节可能会引发如此大的丑闻，以致纳税人会要求进行市政调查。
如果案件因上述两个原因中的任何一个而闭门审理，那么这就是对纳税人的明显背信，负责当局应立即处理此事。如果这纯粹是一起谋杀案，难以想象有什么需要向公众隐瞒的；事实上，为了保护公众自身，应让公众了解基本事实。
我恳切希望警方和报界这种奇怪的缄默能立即停止，从而终结目前围绕这场悲剧进行的疯狂猜测。此致，
正义（JUSTICE）。

PUSI & MERCURY.

OCT 3 1938

Floor Boy Held
In Veksler Case

Comrade Of Suspected
Murderer Arrested;
Inquest Held

Intensive inquiry into the mur-
der of Miss Margaret Veksler, 22
launched by the Settlement police
over the weekend, has resulted in
the arrest of a floor boy employed
by the Broadway Mansions and
the recovery of a pair of blood-
stained trousers.

The actual murderer, believed
to be the cook-boy who disappear-
ed after the killing, was still at
large today, however. The in-
vestigators continued to search for
him all over the city.

Trousers Found

The floor boy was placed under
arrest by Detective Sub-Inspector
M. L. Crowther yesterday, follow-
ing the discovery of the trousers,
a pair of short underpants, one
cotton singlet, a pair of stockings
and a short white jacket in the
apartment in Broadway Mansions
where Miss Veksler was murder-
ed.

During questioning, it was dis-
closed that the blood-stained
trousers belonged to the coolie,
who gave his name as Chu Chin-
doong, 29-year-old native of
Chinghai. He stated that the
trousers were borrowed by the
missing cook. He denied that the
other garments belonged to him.
Both boys shared the same room
in the building, although Chu was
employed by the landlords while
the other was a private cook in
the employ of Captain H. M.
Smyth, deputy commissioner of
the S.M.P., in whose room Miss
Veksler was found murdered.

Death By Violence

Chu was this morning arraign-
ed before the First Special District
Court on a writ of detention.
After a short questioning by
Judge Wong he was ordered de-
tained until next week. Mr. T. Y.
Chang, municipal advocate, gave
evidence.

It was stated by the advocate
that the court procurator during
the inquest returned a verdict of
death by violence and suffocation.
The judicial doctor ventured his
opinion during the inquest, that
the victim's head was bashed in
by a blunt instrument, possibly a
beer bottle, and that she was later
suffocated to death by a blanket,
the advocate stated. The murder

took place between 2 and 5 p.m.
last Friday, according to the
judicial doctor.

Revenge Suggested

The police today advanced the
theory that the murder may have
been prompted by revenge. In
this connection, the arrested man
is being closely questioned as he
has been on intimate terms with
the cook.

Miss Veksler was found murder-
ed in Captain Smyth's room at
Apt. 14, Broadway Mansions, on
Soochow Road, late Friday night.
Drawers had been ransacked and
there were no jewelry on the de-
ceased. There was also evidence
of a desperate struggle. Miss
Veksler had known Captain Smyth
for some time.

Funeral Held

At 2 o'clock yesterday afternoon
simple funeral services were held
at the Hungjao Road Cemetery
for the late Miss Veksler. A
spray of white lilies from Captain
Smyth was lowered into the grave
with the casket. Dean A. C. S.
Trivett of the Cathedral, officiat-
ed.

It is unknown whether the de-
ceased was of the Jewish or
Christian faith as there was
much debating among Miss
Veksler's friends on this point.
Her former husband, Alfred
Haimovitch, was Jewish, but this
does not signify that his wife
was too. A number of Jewish
friends went to the Jewish
Cemetery at 3 p.m., the time set
for the funeral, and then dis-
covered that Miss Veksler had re-
ceived a Christian burial an hour
earlier at Hungjao.

Captain Smyth has made a
statement to the local Jewish
community, it is understood, that
Miss Veksler was given a Chris-
tian burial and that he has taken
full responsibility for it and the
expenses. Jewish leaders here,
however, maintain that Miss
Veksler should have been buried
according to the Jewish faith, as
they declare that she was a Jewess
and that they have documents to
prove it. They say nothing will
be done, however, until and if her
mother, who is in Harbin, arrives
in Shanghai.

普西与墨丘利。

1938年10月3日

楼层服务生因
韦克斯勒案被拘

涉嫌凶手之同伙被捕；
举行验尸讯问

租界警方上周末对22岁的玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Veksler）小姐谋杀案展开密集调查，目前已逮捕一名受雇于百老汇大厦的楼层服务生，并寻获一条沾有血迹的长裤。

然而，据信为案发后失踪的厨役的实际凶手，今日仍在逃。调查人员继续在全市范围内搜捕此人。

发现长裤

继在韦克斯勒小姐遇害的百老汇大厦公寓内发现一条短裤、一件棉质汗衫、一双长袜和一件白色短夹克后，警探副督察 M. L. 克劳瑟（M. L. Crowther）于昨日将该楼层服务生逮捕。

在审讯过程中，获悉那条沾血长裤属于这名苦力，其自报姓名为朱金堂（Chu Chin-doong），29岁，青海人。他称该长裤是被那名失踪的厨师借走的。他否认其他衣物归其所有。这两名青年在大楼内共用同一房间，尽管朱受雇于房东，而另一人则是受雇于上海公共租界工部局警务处副总巡 H. M. 史密斯（H. M. Smyth）上尉的私人厨师，韦克斯勒小姐正是在史密斯上尉的房间内被发现遇害。

死于暴力

朱今晨凭拘留令在第一特区法院受审。经王法官简短讯问后，他被命令羁押至下周。市公廨律师 T. Y. 张出庭作证。

该律师陈述，检察官在验尸讯问中裁定死因为暴力致死及窒息。法医在验尸讯问中提出意见，认为受害者头部遭钝器击打，凶器可能是一个啤酒瓶，随后她被用毯子闷死，律师称。据法医判断，谋杀发生于上周五下午2时至5时之间。

推测为报复

警方今日提出一种理论，认为谋杀可能是由报复心理驱使。就此而言，被捕男子正受到严密讯问，因为他与那名厨师关系密切。

周五深夜，韦克斯勒小姐被发现遇害于苏州路百老汇大厦14号公寓史密斯上尉的房间内。抽屉被翻乱，死者身上没有珠宝。现场也有激烈挣扎的痕迹。韦克斯勒小姐认识史密斯上尉已有一段时间。

举行葬礼

昨日下午2时，在虹桥公墓为已故的韦克斯勒小姐举行了简单的葬礼。史密斯上尉赠送的一束白百合花随棺木放入墓穴。大教堂教长 A. C. S. 特里维特（A. C. S. Trivett）主持了仪式。

目前尚不清楚死者是信奉犹太教还是基督教，因为韦克斯勒小姐的朋友们在此问题上争论不休。她的前夫阿尔弗雷德·海莫维奇（Alfred Haimovitch）是犹太人，但这并不意味着他的妻子也是。许多犹太朋友于下午3时（预定的葬礼时间）前往犹太公墓，随后才发现韦克斯勒小姐已于一小时前在虹桥接受了基督教葬礼。

据悉，史密斯上尉已向当地犹太社区发表声明，称韦克斯勒小姐已按基督教方式安葬，他对此事及相关费用承担全部责任。然而，当地的犹太领袖坚持认为，韦克斯勒小姐应按犹太教仪式安葬，因为他们宣称她是犹太女子，并有文件证明。但他们表示，除非且直到其目前在哈尔滨的母亲抵达上海，否则不会采取任何行动。

October 3, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao (2/10) :-

MURDER OF A FOREIGN GIRL IN THE BROADWAY MANSIONS.

Two days ago, a strange murder case occurred
in Room No. 14 on the 5th floor of Broadway Mansions,
occupied by a certain senior foreign officer of the S.M.C.
The victim is a girl named Miss Margaret Wexler, a white
Russian, a friend of this senior foreign officer. She
was killed by someone with a beer bottle.
The girl was paying a visit at the invitation
of the foreign officer. It happened that the officer
was out and a servant admitted the girl. When the
officer returned, he found the door locked. When the
door was eventually opened, he found the girl had been
murdered. The Police are investigating the case.
It is learned that the deceased was 24 years
of age; her father is a German. She removed to Harbin
from Moscow 12 years ago and later came to Shanghai.
At the time of her death, she resided in the Metropole
Hotel, Foochow Road. She intended to go to England
recently.
Many rumours are in circulation about the
case. Some say that it is a case of common robbery and
that the girl was murdered because she had resisted.
Two Chinese servants are under suspicion.
Another report says that the Russian girl
was a spy of a certain party, but this could not be
confirmed.

《大美晚报》（10月2日）：-

百老汇大厦发生外籍女子谋杀案。

两天前，在百老汇大厦五楼14号房间发生了一起离奇的谋杀案，该房间由工部局某高级外籍官员居住。受害者是一名名叫玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Margaret Wexler）小姐的女子，白俄人，是该高级外籍官员的朋友。她被人用啤酒瓶杀害。
该女子是应这位外籍官员的邀请前来拜访的。碰巧官员外出，一名仆人让该女子进入。当官员返回时，发现门被锁住。最终打开门后，他发现该女子已被谋杀。警方正在调查此案。
据悉，死者年24岁；其父为德国人。她于12年前从莫斯科迁居哈尔滨，后来来到上海。去世时，她居住在福州路的大都会酒店。她最近打算前往英国。
关于此案流传着许多谣言。有人说这是一起普通的抢劫案，该女子因反抗而被杀。两名中国仆役受到怀疑。
另有报告称，这名俄国女子是某党派的间谍，但此说法无法证实。

October 3, 1938

The effeminate-complexioned youth above, for whom the S.M. Police have posted a $250 reward, is Yu Yeh-yuen, aged 18 to 20, cook employed by Captain Smyth, S.M.P. Commissioner. He is wanted for the murder of 22-year-old Russian-Jewish Marguerite Veksler Friday between 2 and 5 p.m.

Police Post Reward Of $250
For Arrest Of Chinese Cook,
Wanted For Veksler Murder

Japanese Report Girl Was Spy Ridiculed By All Intimate Friends; Inquest Reveals Death Is Caused By Violence, Suffocation

The Shanghai Municipal Police yesterday posted a $250 reward for the arrest or information leading to the arrest of Yu Yeh-yuen, aged 18 to 20, baby-faced cook employed by Captain H.M. Smyth, Deputy Commissioner S.M.P. The youth is wanted for the death of 22-year-old Russian-Jewish Marguerite Veksler, who was found brutally murdered in Captain Smyth's Broadway Mansions apartment late Friday night.

Another new angle on the case, which is not being seriously considered, is the report of Japanese origin that Miss Veksler was employed as a spy. This report was reduced to a grim jest by the unanimous ridicule of friends of the deceased.

In the First Special District Court yesterday morning the police arraigned before the tribunal 29-year-old Chu Chin-doong, floor boy employed by the management of Broadway Mansions who was arrested Sunday following the discovery in his room of a pair of blood-stained trousers.

Shared Room

Chu shared his room in the servants' quarters with the wanted murderer, "Baby-Face" Yu, and told the court yesterday that the trousers were his property, but that they had been borrowed by Yu. Both Chu and Yu are natives of Chinghai.

1938年10月3日

上述面色阴柔的青年，即上海公共租界警务处悬赏250元通缉的对象，是俞逸源，年龄18至20岁，系上海公共租界警务处副总巡史密斯上尉雇佣的厨师。他因涉嫌于周五下午2时至5时之间谋杀22岁的俄籍犹太女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒（Marguerite Veksler）而被通缉。

警方悬赏250元
通缉涉嫌韦克斯勒谋杀案的中国厨师

日方报道称女孩为间谍的说法遭到所有亲密朋友的嘲笑；验尸讯问揭示死因为暴力及窒息

上海公共租界警务处于昨日张贴悬赏250元的告示，以求逮捕或获取导致逮捕俞逸源的线索。俞逸源，18至20岁，面容稚嫩，系上海公共租界警务处副总巡 H. M. 史密斯上尉雇佣的厨师。该青年因涉嫌造成22岁的俄籍犹太女子玛格丽特·韦克斯勒死亡而被通缉，韦克斯勒于周五深夜在史密斯上尉位于百老汇大厦的公寓内被发现惨遭谋杀。

关于此案的另一个新角度（并未被严肃考虑）是一则源自日本的报道，称韦克斯勒小姐受雇为间谍。这一报道遭到了死者朋友们一致的嘲笑，沦为残酷的笑话。

昨日上午在第一特区法院，警方将29岁的朱金堂（Chu Chin-doong）提堂受审。朱系百老汇大厦管理处雇佣的楼层服务生，于周日在其房间内发现一条沾血长裤后被捕。

共用房间

朱与被通缉的凶手、“娃娃脸”俞在仆人宿舍共用一间房，并于昨日向法庭陈述，长裤是他的财产，但是被俞借走的。朱和俞均为青海人。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 4 1938

During the hearing, in which the judge ordered Chu to be detained for a week pending investigation, it was revealed that the verdict handed down in the inquest Saturday—which was held in camera—was death by violence and suffocation. The murder was committed between the hours of 2 and 5 p.m. Friday, according to the judicial doctor, and was caused by a blunt instrument, possibly a beer bottle. Later, she was suffocated to death by a blanket.

Police forward a theory that the motive was robbery and personal vengeance. Yu is said to have been stealing for some time, and not long ago Miss Veksler, who caught him in the act, threatened to expose him.

When Captain Smyth entered the apartment Friday night he found Miss Veksler dead, lying on the floor with congealed blood on her head and face. Subsequently it was established that there were seven wounds on her head and face.

The drawers in the room had been ransacked, and all jewelry on the deceased was removed. There was also evidence of a brief but desperate struggle.

Local Jews Indignant

Meanwhile, Shanghai's Jewish community continued to wax indignant yesterday over the fact that Miss Veksler, who was known to all her intimate friends as being of Jewish faith, was buried Sunday in the Hungjao Road Cemetery and not the Jewish Cemetery on Baikal Road. She was given a Christian burial with Dean A.C.S. Trivett of the Holy Trinity Cathedral officiating.

The funeral was scheduled for 3 p.m. at the Baikal Road Cemetery, but the remains of Miss Veksler were buried an hour earlier in Hungjao, leaving a large number of the deceased's Jewish friends who proceeded to the Baikal Road burial ground puzzled.

The local Rabbi is said to have evidence to the effect that Miss Veksler was of Jewish faith. However, it is reported that Captain Smyth has made a statement to the local Jewish community that he assumes full responsibility for the Christian burial and the expenses entailed.

The question of burial will not be brought up unless the deceased's mother, now in Harbin, arrives here and wishes to carry the matter further.

周五晚上，当史密斯上尉进入公寓时，发现韦克斯勒小姐已死亡，躺在地板上，头部和面部有凝固的血迹。随后确认，她的头部和面部共有七处伤口。

房间内的抽屉被翻乱，死者身上的所有珠宝均被取走。现场也有短暂但激烈挣扎的痕迹。

当地犹太人感到愤慨

与此同时，上海犹太社区昨日继续因韦克斯勒小姐一事而感到愤慨。在她所有亲密朋友眼中，她是犹太教徒，但她却在周日被安葬于虹桥公墓，而非贝加尔路（Baikal Road）的犹太公墓。她接受了基督教葬礼，由圣三一大教堂教长 A.C.S. 特里维特主持。

葬礼原定于下午3时在贝加尔路公墓举行，但韦克斯勒小姐的遗体提前一小时在虹桥下葬，致使大批前往贝加尔路墓地的死者犹太朋友感到困惑。

据悉，当地拉比持有证据，证明韦克斯勒小姐信奉犹太教。然而，据报道，史密斯上尉已向当地犹太社区发表声明，称他对基督教葬礼及相关费用承担全部责任。

除非死者的母亲（现居哈尔滨）抵达此地并希望进一步处理此事，否则埋葬问题不会再被提起。
